verdict_reason: The three exponents are computed as the paper defines them and the R/S kernel is exact: on a matched window grid BLME's Hurst estimator is BIT-IDENTICAL to the released nolds.hurst_rs (max absolute difference 0.000e+00 over 128 fractional-Gaussian-noise realizations), and against exact Davies-Harte fGn at H = 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.9 with N=8192 the estimates are 0.3606 / 0.5211 / 0.7070 / 0.8484 (bias +0.066 / +0.029 / +0.004 / -0.048, ordinary finite-series R/S bias). The exponents are exactly scale-free -- max |dH| 0.000e+00, |dJ| 2.220e-16, |dS| 0.000e+00 across scale_ladder(2,1024) -- and translation-free in float64 (|dH| <= 8.1e-10 at +1e3/+1e6/+1e9).
comparable_reason: The headline is now a POOLED fit over per-document-normalised increments, which is the right estimand, but at the shipped config it rests on 5 documents: num_samples=100 counts DOCUMENTS built by joining corpus rows to >=4096 tokens, while core.py sizes the shared corpus at 200 ROWS, so _meta_n_documents = 5 and n_tokens_in_stream = 4475 on 5/5 models. A paired document bootstrap (B=500, same 5 documents) gives a bootstrap sd of H of 0.0101-0.0202 against an observed cross-model H range of only 0.0394 -- 2.4x -- and the 5-model ORDERING is unstable: 22 distinct orders in 500 draws, modal order 34.6%, mean Spearman(bootstrap, observed) +0.645 +/- 0.401. The exponents themselves are dimensionless and architecture-free; the sample is the limit.

confounds_reason: Over 5 models: H rho -0.447 with d_model, -0.369 with n_layers, -0.200 with parameter count and +0.866 with vocab_size; J rho +0.632 with n_layers and +0.600 with parameter count; S rho +0.264 / +0.300. The exponents are dimensionless power-law slopes with no architectural ceiling, so I see no mechanical size proxy -- but with a bootstrap sd of 0.016 against a cross-model range of 0.039 this panel cannot resolve a real association either.
